shortDescription: British sports and fashion retailer JD Sports LSE:JD. cut its profit outlook for the second time in four months on Thursday after a 2.6% fall in third-quarter like-for-like sales, though trading did improve in its key North American market.($1 = 0.7614 pounds)

children: British sports and fashion retailer JD Sports
cut its profit outlook for the second time in four months on Thursday after a 2.6% fall in third-quarter like-for-like sales, though trading did improve in its key North American market.
JD Sports forecast a year to end-January 2027 profit before tax and adjusting items of £700 million to £750 million ($919-$985 million). Its previous guidance was £700 million to £800 million
Prior to Thursday's update, analysts were on average forecasting £723 million. It made £852 million in 2025/26
Group organic sales for the 13 weeks to October 31 fell 1.1%while like-for-like sales fell 2.6%, having been down 3.1% in its second quarter
Like-for-like sales in the key North America market, where the group makes over a third of total sales, fell 2.2%, having been down 6.8% in the second quarter
Like-for-like sales fell 2.7% in Europe, 2.6% in the UK and 5.3% in Asia Pacific
Saw resilient sales trends in apparel and accessories, despite unseasonably warm weather delaying autumn/winter demand
Footwear remained soft given ongoing product cycle evolution, amidst a continued promotional market
Trading in Europe was affected by civil unrest, it said
The outcome also reflects cost-of-living pressures on JD's core young and less affluent customer base and a lack of innovation from Nike
- JD's most important brand partner which is struggling to overhaul its business
Shares in JD are up 12% so far this year but down on a two-year basis
